verses.original: וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מְיֻדָּע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ אִ֚ישׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל מִמִּשְׁפַּ֖חַת אֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ וּשְׁמ֖וֹ בֹּֽעַז׃
verses.transliteration: ū·lə·nā·‘o·mî mə·yud·då̄ʿ lə·’î·šāh ’îš gib·bō·wr ḥa·yil mim·miš·pa·ḥaṯ ’ĕ·lî·me·leḵ ū·šə·mōw bō·‘az
verses.literal: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech whose name was Boaz
verses.literalPt: E TINHA Noemi um parente de seu marido, homem valente e poderoso, da família de Elimeleque; e era o seu nome Boaz.

verses.original: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶֽל־ נָעֳמִ֗י אֵֽלְכָה־ נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣ה בַשִׁבֳּלִ֔ים אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶמְצָא־ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer rūṯ ham·mō·w·’ă·ḇî·yāh ’el- nā·‘o·mî ’ê·lə·ḵāh- nā haś·śā·ḏeh wa·ʾă·la·qoṭ·ṭå̄h ḇa·šib·bo·līm ’a·ḥar ’ă·šer ’em·ṣā- ḥên bə·‘ê·nāw wat·tō·mer lāh lə·ḵî ḇit·tî
verses.literal: And Ruth the Moabitess . . . said to Naomi Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor Go ahead my daughter Naomi replied
verses.literalPt: E Rute, a moabita, disse a Noemi: Deixa-me ir ao campo, e apanharei espigas atrás daquele em cujos olhos eu achar graça. E ela disse: Vai, minha filha.

verses.original: וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקֹּצְרִ֑ים וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֱלִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tê·leḵ wat·tā·ḇō·w wat·tə·laq·qêṭ baś·śā·ḏeh ’a·ḥă·rê haq·qō·ṣə·rîm way·yi·qer miq·re·hā ḥel·qaṯ haś·śā·ḏeh lə·ḇō·‘az ’ă·šer mim·miš·pa·ḥaṯ ’ĕ·lî·me·leḵ
verses.literal: So Ruth departed and went out into the field and gleaned after the harvesters And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz who was from the clan of Elimelech
verses.literalPt: Foi, pois, e chegou, e apanhava espigas no campo após os segadores; e caiu-lhe em sorte uma parte do campo de Boaz, que era da família de Elimeleque.

verses.original: וְהִנֵּה־ בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א מִבֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh- ḇō·‘az bā mib·bêṯ le·ḥem way·yō·mer laq·qō·wṣ·rîm Yah·weh ‘im·mā·ḵem way·yō·mə·rū lōw yə·ḇā·reḵ·ḵā Yah·weh
verses.literal: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters The LORD be with you The LORD bless you they replied
verses.literalPt: E eis que Boaz veio de Belém, e disse aos segadores: O SENHOR seja convosco. E disseram-lhe eles: O SENHOR te abençoe.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בֹּ֙עַז֙ לְנַעֲר֔וֹ הַנִּצָּ֖ב עַל־ הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֑ים לְמִ֖י הַנַּעֲרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer bō·‘az lə·na·‘ă·rōw han·niṣ·ṣāḇ ‘al- haq·qō·wṣ·rîm lə·mî han·na·‘ă·rāh haz·zōṯ
verses.literal: And Boaz asked the foreman . . . of his harvesters Whose young woman is this
verses.literalPt: Depois disse Boaz a seu moço, que estava posto sobre os segadores: De quem é esta moça?

verses.original: וַיַּ֗עַן הַנַּ֛עַר הַנִּצָּ֥ב עַל־ הַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נַעֲרָ֤ה מֽוֹאֲבִיָּה֙ הִ֔יא הַשָּׁ֥בָה עִֽם־ נָעֳמִ֖י מִשְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an han·na·‘ar han·niṣ·ṣāḇ ‘al- haq·qō·wṣ·rîm way·yō·mar na·‘ă·rāh mō·w·’ă·ḇî·yāh hî haš·šā·ḇāh ‘im- nā·‘o·mî miś·śə·ḏêh mō·w·’āḇ
verses.literal: The foreman . . . . . . . . . . . . answered She is the Moabitess . . . who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab
verses.literalPt: E respondeu o moço, que estava posto sobre os segadores, e disse: Esta é a moça moabita que voltou com Noemi dos campos de Moabe.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲלַקֳטָה־ נָּא֙ וְאָסַפְתִּ֣י בָֽעֳמָרִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקּוֹצְרִ֑ים וַתָּב֣וֹא וַֽתַּעֲמ֗וֹד מֵאָ֤ז הַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וְעַד־ עַ֔תָּה זֶ֛ה שִׁבְתָּ֥הּ הַבַּ֖יִת מְעָֽט׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer ’ă·la·qo·ṭāh- nā wə·’ā·sap̄·tî ḇā·‘o·mā·rîm ’a·ḥă·rê haq·qō·wṣ·rîm wat·tā·ḇō·w wat·ta·‘ă·mō·wḏ mê·’āz hab·bō·qer wə·‘aḏ- ‘at·tāh zeh šiḇ·tāh hab·ba·yiṯ mə·‘āṭ
verses.literal: She has said Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters So she came out and has continued from morning until now except that she rested a short time in the shelter
verses.literalPt: Disse-me ela: Deixa-me colher espigas, e ajuntá-las entre as gavelas após os segadores. Assim ela veio, e desde pela manhã está aqui até agora, a não ser um pouco que esteve sentada em casa.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל־ ר֜וּת הֲל֧וֹא שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ בִּתִּ֗י אַל־ תֵּלְכִי֙ לִלְקֹט֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה אַחֵ֔ר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א תַעֲבוּרִ֖י מִזֶּ֑ה וְכֹ֥ה תִדְבָּקִ֖ין עִם־ נַעֲרֹתָֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer bō·‘az ’el- rūṯ hă·lō·w šā·ma·‘at bit·tî ’al- tê·lə·ḵî lil·qōṭ bə·śā·ḏeh ’a·ḥêr wə·ḡam lō ṯa·‘ă·ḇū·rî miz·zeh wə·ḵōh ṯiḏ·bā·qîn ‘im- na·‘ă·rō·ṯāy
verses.literal: Then Boaz said to Ruth Listen my daughter Do not go and glean in another field and do not go away from this place but stay here close to my servant girls
verses.literalPt: Então disse Boaz a Rute: Ouves, filha minha; não vás colher em outro campo, nem tampouco passes daqui; porém aqui ficarás com as minhas moças.

verses.original: עֵינַ֜יִךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־ יִקְצֹרוּן֙ וְהָלַ֣כְתִּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן הֲל֥וֹא צִוִּ֛יתִי אֶת־ הַנְּעָרִ֖ים לְבִלְתִּ֣י נָגְעֵ֑ךְ וְצָמִ֗ת וְהָלַכְתְּ֙ אֶל־ הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְשָׁתִ֕ית מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאֲב֖וּן הַנְּעָרִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: ‘ê·na·yiḵ baś·śā·ḏeh ’ă·šer- yiq·ṣō·rūn wə·hå̄·laḵ·ti ’a·ḥă·rê·hen hă·lō·w ṣiw·wî·ṯî ’eṯ- han·nə·‘ā·rîm lə·ḇil·tî nā·ḡə·‘êḵ wə·ṣā·miṯ wə·hā·laḵt ’el- hak·kê·lîm wə·šā·ṯîṯ mê·’ă·šer yiš·’ă·ḇūn han·nə·‘ā·rîm
verses.literal: Let your eyes be on the field they are harvesting and follow along after these girls Indeed I have ordered the young men not to touch you And when you are thirsty go . . . and drink from the jars the young men have filled
verses.literalPt: Os teus olhos estarão atentos no campo que segarem, e irás após elas; não dei ordem aos moços, que não te molestem? Tendo tu sede, vai aos vasos, e bebe do que os moços tirarem.

verses.original: וַתִּפֹּל֙ עַל־ פָּנֶ֔יהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו מַדּוּעַ֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ לְהַכִּירֵ֔נִי וְאָּנֹכִ֖י נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tip·pōl ‘al- pā·ne·hā wat·tiš·ta·ḥū ’ā·rə·ṣāh wat·tō·mer ’ê·lāw mad·dū·a‘ mā·ṣā·ṯî ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā lə·hak·kî·rê·nî wəʾ·ʾå̄·nō·ḵī nā·ḵə·rî·yāh
verses.literal: At this, she fell on her face bowing low to the ground and said to him Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me even though I am a foreigner
verses.literalPt: Então ela caiu sobre o seu rosto, e se inclinou à terra; e disse-lhe: Por que achei graça em teus olhos, para que faças caso de mim, sendo eu uma estrangeira?

verses.original: וַיַּ֤עַן בֹּ֙עַז֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ הֻגֵּ֨ד הֻגַּ֜ד לִ֗י כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂית֙ אֶת־ חֲמוֹתֵ֔ךְ אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ וַתַּֽעַזְבִ֞י אָּבִ֣יךְ וְאִמֵּ֗ךְ וְאֶ֙רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔ךְ וַתֵּ֣לְכִ֔י אֶל־ עַ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יָדַ֖עַתְּ תְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an bō·‘az way·yō·mer lāh hug·gêḏ hug·gaḏ lî kōl ’ă·šer- ‘ā·śîṯ ’eṯ- ḥă·mō·w·ṯêḵ ’a·ḥă·rê mō·wṯ ’î·šêḵ wat·ta·‘az·ḇî ʾå̄·ḇīḵ wə·’im·mêḵ wə·’e·reṣ mō·w·laḏ·têḵ wat·tê·lə·ḵî ’el- ‘am ’ă·šer lō- yā·ḏa·‘at tə·mō·wl šil·šō·wm
verses.literal: Boaz replied . . . . . . I have been made fully aware . . . . . . of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth and how you came to a people you did not know before . . .
verses.literalPt: E respondeu Boaz, e disse-lhe: Bem se me contou quanto fizeste à tua sogra, depois da morte de teu marido; e deixaste a teu pai e a tua mãe, e a terra onde nasceste, e vieste para um povo que antes não conheceste.

verses.original: יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה פָּעֳלֵ֑ךְ וּתְהִ֨י מַשְׂכֻּרְתֵּ֜ךְ שְׁלֵמָ֗ה מֵעִ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֖את לַחֲס֥וֹת תַּֽחַת־ כְּנָפָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: yə·šal·lêm Yah·weh pā·‘o·lêḵ ū·ṯə·hî maś·kur·têḵ šə·lê·māh mê·‘im Yah·weh ’ĕ·lō·hê yiś·rā·’êl ’ă·šer- bāṯ la·ḥă·sō·wṯ ta·ḥaṯ- kə·nā·p̄āw
verses.literal: May the LORD repay your work and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD the God of Israel under whose wings you have taken refuge
verses.literalPt: O SENHOR retribua o teu feito; e te seja concedido pleno galardão da parte do SENHOR Deus de Israel, sob cujas asas te vieste abrigar.

verses.original: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר אֶמְצָא־ חֵ֨ן בְּעֵינֶ֤יךָ אֲדֹנִי֙ כִּ֣י נִֽחַמְתָּ֔נִי וְכִ֥י דִבַּ֖רְתָּ עַל־ לֵ֣ב שִׁפְחָתֶ֑ךָ וְאָנֹכִי֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽהְיֶ֔ה כְּאַחַ֖ת שִׁפְחֹתֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer ’em·ṣā- ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā ’ă·ḏō·nî kî ni·ḥam·tā·nî wə·ḵî ḏib·bar·tā ‘al- lêḇ šip̄·ḥā·ṯe·ḵā wə·’ā·nō·ḵî lō ’eh·yeh kə·’a·ḥaṯ šip̄·ḥō·ṯe·ḵā
verses.literal: My lord she said may I continue to find favor in your eyes for you have comforted . . . and spoken kindly to your maidservant though I am not like one of your servant girls
verses.literalPt: E disse ela: Ache eu graça em teus olhos, SENHOR meu, pois me consolaste, e falaste ao coração da tua serva, não sendo eu ainda como uma das tuas criadas.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨ה בֹ֜עַז לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל גֹּ֤שִֽׁי הֲלֹם֙ וְאָכַ֣לְתְּ מִן־ הַלֶּ֔חֶם וְטָבַ֥לְתְּ פִּתֵּ֖ךְ בַּחֹ֑מֶץ וַתֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ מִצַּ֣ד הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֔ים וַיִּצְבָּט־ לָ֣הּ קָלִ֔י וַתֹּ֥אכַל וַתִּשְׂבַּ֖ע וַתֹּתַֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lāh ḇō·‘az lə·‘êṯ hā·’ō·ḵel gō·šî hă·lōm wə·’ā·ḵalt min- hal·le·ḥem wə·ṭā·ḇalt pit·têḵ ba·ḥō·meṣ wat·tê·šeḇ miṣ·ṣaḏ haq·qō·wṣ·rîm way·yiṣ·bāṭ- lāh qā·lî wat·tō·ḵal wat·tiś·ba‘ wat·tō·ṯar
verses.literal: At mealtime . . . Boaz said to her Come over here have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce So she sat down beside the harvesters and he offered her roasted grain and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over
verses.literalPt: E, sendo já hora de comer, disse-lhe Boaz: Achega-te aqui, e come do pão, e molha o teu bocado no vinagre. E ela se assentou ao lado dos segadores, e ele lhe deu do trigo tostado, e comeu, e se fartou, e ainda lhe sobejou.

verses.original: וַתָּ֖קָם לְלַקֵּ֑ט וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת־ נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ין הָֽעֳמָרִ֛ים תְּלַקֵּ֖ט וְלֹ֥א תַכְלִימֽוּהָ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tā·qām lə·laq·qêṭ way·ṣaw bō·‘az ’eṯ- nə·‘ā·rāw lê·mōr gam bên hā·‘o·mā·rîm tə·laq·qêṭ wə·lō ṯaḵ·lî·mū·hā
verses.literal: When Ruth got up to glean Boaz ordered his young men . . . Even if she gathers among the sheaves do not insult her
verses.literalPt: E, levantando-se ela a colher, Boaz deu ordem aos seus moços, dizendo: Até entre as gavelas deixai-a colher, e não a censureis.

verses.original: וְגַ֛ם שֹׁל־ תָּשֹׁ֥לּוּ לָ֖הּ מִן־ הַצְּבָתִ֑ים וַעֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם וְלִקְּטָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִגְעֲרוּ־ בָֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḡam šōl- tā·šōl·lū lāh min- haṣ·ṣə·ḇā·ṯîm wa·‘ă·zaḇ·tem wə·liq·qə·ṭāh wə·lō ṯiḡ·‘ă·rū- ḇāh
verses.literal: Rather pull out . . . for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather Do not rebuke her
verses.literalPt: E deixai cair alguns punhados, e deixai-os ficar, para que os colha, e não a repreendais.

verses.original: וַתְּלַקֵּ֥ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה עַד־ הָעָ֑רֶב וַתַּחְבֹּט֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ לִקֵּ֔טָה וַיְהִ֖י כְּאֵיפָ֥ה שְׂעֹרִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tə·laq·qêṭ baś·śā·ḏeh ‘aḏ- hā·‘ā·reḇ wat·taḥ·bōṭ ’êṯ ’ă·šer- liq·qê·ṭāh way·hî kə·’ê·p̄āh śə·‘ō·rîm
verses.literal: So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening And when she beat out what she had gleaned it was about an ephah of barley
verses.literalPt: E esteve ela apanhando naquele campo até à tarde; e debulhou o que apanhou, e foi quase um efa de cevada.

verses.original: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ וַתָּב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וַתֵּ֥רֶא חֲמוֹתָ֖הּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ לִקֵּ֑טָה וַתּוֹצֵא֙ וַתִּתֶּן־ לָ֔הּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹתִ֖רָה מִשָּׂבְעָֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tiś·śā wat·tā·ḇō·w hā·‘îr wat·tê·re ḥă·mō·w·ṯāh ’êṯ ’ă·šer- liq·qê·ṭāh wat·tō·w·ṣê wat·tit·ten- lāh ’êṯ ’ă·šer- hō·w·ṯi·rāh miś·śā·ḇə·‘āh
verses.literal: She picked up the grain and went into the town where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi
verses.literalPt: E tomou-a, e veio à cidade; e viu sua sogra o que tinha apanhado; também tirou, e deu-lhe o que sobejara depois de fartar-se.

verses.original: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨הּ חֲמוֹתָ֜הּ אֵיפֹ֨ה לִקַּ֤טְתְּ הַיּוֹם֙ וְאָ֣נָה עָשִׂ֔ית יְהִ֥י מַכִּירֵ֖ךְ בָּר֑וּךְ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לַחֲמוֹתָ֗הּ אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשְׂתָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֧יתִי עִמּ֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם בֹּֽעַז׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer lāh ḥă·mō·w·ṯāh ’ê·p̄ōh liq·qaṭt hay·yō·wm wə·’ā·nāh ‘ā·śîṯ yə·hî mak·kî·rêḵ bā·rūḵ wat·tag·gêḏ la·ḥă·mō·w·ṯāh ’êṯ ’ă·šer- ‘ā·śə·ṯāh ‘im·mōw wat·tō·mer šêm hā·’îš ’ă·šer ‘ā·śî·ṯî ‘im·mōw hay·yō·wm bō·‘az
verses.literal: Then her mother-in-law asked her Where did you glean today and where did you work Blessed be the man who noticed you So she told her mother-in-law where she had worked The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz she said
verses.literalPt: Então disse-lhe sua sogra: Onde colheste hoje, e onde trabalhaste? Bendito seja aquele que te reconheceu. E relatou à sua sogra com quem tinha trabalhado, e disse: O nome do homem com quem hoje trabalhei é Boaz.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְכַלָּתָ֗הּ בָּר֥וּךְ הוּא֙ לַיהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־ עָזַ֣ב חַסְדּ֔וֹ אֶת־ הַחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־ הַמֵּתִ֑ים וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ נָעֳמִ֗י קָר֥וֹב לָ֙נוּ֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ מִֽגֹּאֲלֵ֖נוּ הֽוּא׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer nā·‘o·mî lə·ḵal·lā·ṯāh bā·rūḵ hū Yah·weh ’ă·šer lō- ‘ā·zaḇ ḥas·dōw ’eṯ- ha·ḥay·yîm wə·’eṯ- ham·mê·ṯîm wat·tō·mer lāh nā·‘o·mî qā·rō·wḇ lā·nū hā·’îš mig·gō·’ă·lê·nū hū
verses.literal: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law May he be blessed by the LORD who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living . . . or the dead Naomi continued The man is a close relative He is one of our kinsman-redeemers
verses.literalPt: Então Noemi disse à sua nora: Bendito seja ele do SENHOR, que ainda não tem deixado a sua beneficência nem para com os vivos nem para com os mortos. Disse-lhe mais Noemi: Este homem é nosso parente chegado, e um dentre os nossos remidores.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֑ה גַּ֣ם׀ כִּי־ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֗י עִם־ הַנְּעָרִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־ לִי֙ תִּדְבָּקִ֔ין עַ֣ד אִם־ כִּלּ֔וּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַקָּצִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־ לִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer rūṯ ham·mō·w·’ă·ḇî·yāh gam kî- ’ā·mar ’ê·lay ‘im- han·nə·‘ā·rîm ’ă·šer- lî tiḏ·bā·qîn ‘aḏ ’im- kil·lū ’êṯ kāl- haq·qā·ṣîr ’ă·šer- lî
verses.literal: Then Ruth the Moabitess said He also . . . told me . . . Stay with my young men - until . . . they have finished gathering all my harvest
verses.literalPt: E disse Rute, a moabita: Também ainda me disse: Com os moços que tenho te ajuntarás, até que acabem toda a sega que tenho.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר נָעֳמִ֖י אֶל־ ר֣וּת כַּלָּתָ֑הּ ט֣וֹב בִּתִּ֗י כִּ֤י תֵֽצְאִי֙ עִם־ נַ֣עֲרוֹתָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִפְגְּעוּ־ בָ֖ךְ בְּשָׂדֶ֥ה אַחֵֽר׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer nā·‘o·mî ’el- rūṯ kal·lā·ṯāh ṭō·wḇ bit·tî kî ṯê·ṣə·’î ‘im- na·‘ă·rō·w·ṯāw wə·lō yip̄·gə·‘ū- ḇāḵ bə·śā·ḏeh ’a·ḥêr
verses.literal: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth My daughter . . . it is good for you to work with his young women so that nothing will happen to you in another field
verses.literalPt: E disse Noemi a sua nora: Melhor é, filha minha, que saias com as suas moças, para que noutro campo não te encontrem.

verses.original: וַתִּדְבַּ֞ק בְּנַעֲר֥וֹת בֹּ֙עַז֙ לְלַקֵּ֔ט עַד־ כְּל֥וֹת קְצִֽיר־ הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־ חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tiḏ·baq bə·na·‘ă·rō·wṯ bō·‘az lə·laq·qêṭ ‘aḏ- kə·lō·wṯ qə·ṣîr- haś·śə·‘ō·rîm ū·qə·ṣîr ha·ḥiṭ·ṭîm wat·tê·šeḇ ’eṯ- ḥă·mō·w·ṯāh
verses.literal: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain until the barley . . . and wheat harvests were finished And she lived with her mother-in-law
verses.literalPt: Assim, ajuntou-se com as moças de Boaz, para colher até que a sega das cevadas e dos trigos se acabou; e ficou com a sua sogra.
